Dear Sir/Madam,  I am writing on behalf of Neguinho Motors Ltd, the registered keeper and legal owner of the vehicle with registration number AP23OOH.  We have received a serious complaint from a former hirer who was issued a Penalty Charge Notice (GX27513068) dated 15/07/2025, despite the fact that their hire contract with us was officially terminated on 12/05/2025. A Termination Confirmation Letter was issued to him, and the vehicle was re-allocated under a new hire agreement to different client on following week.  Importantly, the V5C document remains in the name of Neguinho Motors Ltd, and therefore, we are and remain the registered keeper. Under Regulation 27 of the Road Vehicles (Registration and Licensing) Regulations 2002, TfL is legally required to request keeper details from the DVLA in order to identify the correct party for enforcement action.  In this case, it appears TfL failed to do so correctly and issued the PCN to an individual who was no longer liable, causing:  Reputational harm to our company;  Loss of a longstanding client;  Misattribution of liability, which may amount to a data processing failure.  We urge you to:  Investigate how the PCN was issued to the incorrect party;  Redirect or cancel the PCN in accordance with the actual registered keeper status;  Confirm in writing the outcome of your internal review and corrective action.  For your reference, we are attaching:  The hire termination letter dated 12/05/2025;  Proof that Neguinho Motors Ltd is the registered keeper;  Documentation of the new hire agreement starting 12/05/2025.  Please treat this matter as urgent. Should no satisfactory response be received within 7 working days, we reserve the right to escalate the matter to the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) and seek further legal remedy for the reputational and financial damages caused.
